content.user_title: Authenticate TypeScript Apps with Azure Identity
content.value_statement: Azure authentication choices can be hard to apply across local and cloud environments. This skill gives concise TypeScript guidance for Azure Identity credentials and token flows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure Identity package for TypeScript projects.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential and its common credential chain order.
Covers managed identity, service principal, browser, and device code credentials.
Describes sovereign cloud authority hosts and bearer token provider usage.
Lists key Azure Identity and Azure core authentication types.
Includes Azure logger guidance for authentication troubleshooting.
limitations: Does not run authentication flows or validate Azure tenant settings.
Does not replace current Azure SDK documentation for version-specific changes.
Uses placeholders that users must replace and protect.
Does not cover every Azure service client or enterprise policy.

use_cases.title: Set Up Local Development Auth
use_cases.description: Choose a credential flow that works for TypeScript development without hardcoded secrets.

use_cases.title: Plan Cloud Deployment Identity
use_cases.description: Compare managed identity and service principal patterns for deployed Azure workloads.

use_cases.title: Review Azure SDK Auth Choices
use_cases.description: Confirm which credential classes fit browser, CLI, device, and token provider scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Credential
prompt_templates.prompt: Use azure-identity-ts to recommend an Azure Identity credential for my TypeScript app. My app runs locally and in Azure App Service.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Secret Auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use azure-identity-ts to explain how to move from client secret authentication to managed identity in a TypeScript service.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Credential Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Use azure-identity-ts to design a credential chain for local development, CI, and production. Include security tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Token Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use azure-identity-ts to debug an Azure SDK token acquisition failure in TypeScript. Ask for missing tenant, client, and runtime details first.

output_examples.input: How should my local tool and deployed service authenticate to Azure Blob Storage?
output_examples.output: Use DefaultAzureCredential during development and managed identity in Azure. Assign the identity the least required Blob role.

output_examples.input: When should I use a service principal certificate instead of a client secret?
output_examples.output: Use certificates when policy requires stronger credential handling. Store certificate files securely and rotate them through approved operations.

output_examples.input: My token request fails in Azure Government. What should I check?
output_examples.output: Confirm the authority host, tenant, scope, and credential type. Sovereign clouds need the matching Azure authority host.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity for production workloads when the Azure host supports it.
Use DefaultAzureCredential to align local development and deployed environments.
Grant only the Azure roles required by the service operation.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode tenant IDs, client IDs, secrets, tokens, or certificate passwords in source files.
Do not use interactive browser or device code flows for unattended production services.
Do not log access tokens, credential objects, or authentication error payloads with secrets.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps choose and apply Azure Identity credential patterns in TypeScript applications.

faq.question: Does it authenticate to Azure for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must configure Azure identities and permissions.

faq.question: Is DefaultAzureCredential always the right choice?
faq.answer: No. It is a strong default, but some environments need explicit credential configuration.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata marks the skill as compatible with all three tools.

faq.question: Does it cover managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes system-assigned and user-assigned managed identity patterns.

faq.question: How should I handle secrets when using these examples?
faq.answer: Use managed identity when possible. Store required secrets in approved secret management systems.
